answers.question: My club mate runs 70 miles a week before a marathon. I'm thinking of doubling to 80 next week to catch up, running twice a day. Would that work?
answers.answer:
No, do not double up to 80 miles with doubles next week. You are at 40 miles now, were at 30 before the build, and your longest week ever was 53. Jumping to 80 would roughly double your current load in seven days, which is the single biggest predictor of injury in marathon prep. Your club mate built to 70 over months or years, not in a week.

What actually drives a sub-3:45 is not raw mileage but a strong long run, one honest quality session, and showing up healthy on Nov 1. You are hitting all three. Trust the plan: we will peak around 47 – 50 miles this week with a 20 miler, then taper. That beats a crash course at 80 every time.

new.analysis:
## Why this plan

You executed the week cleanly: every session done, distances to the metre, and the marathon-pace reps landed at goal pace with a sensible drift. That is exactly the engagement a build phase needs five weeks out.

The jump is in the long run and the quality volume, not the training days. We go from 15 to 20 miles on Sunday because the 20 miler three weeks back was solid and your recovery long run cleared the legs. Midweek we extend the marathon-pace block from 6 to 7 continuous miles, so you get a longer continuous spell at race effort while the overall session stays controlled.

Easy days stay genuinely easy, HR under 145, because the Wednesday and Sunday loads do the real work. Keep the Brooks Ghost for easy and long, the Endorphin Speed for the marathon-pace reps if you prefer, and treat Mon and Fri as full rest. If anything feels off after the long run, tell me on Sunday night rather than pushing through on Tuesday.
